title: Agent Incident Atlas incident record
description: One anonymized record of an agentic AI failure in a production or pilot enterprise setting. Version 0.1.0. See schema/FIELDS.md for guidance on filling each field.

partialDate.description: YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Prefer month precision to reduce re-identification risk.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record conforms to.

id.description: Unique identifier, AIA-<year added>-<three digit sequence>. Also the file name (AIA-2026-001.json).

seed.description: True only for illustrative composite records written by the maintainers. Community submissions must be false.

provenance.description: Where the record comes from. composite-illustration is reserved for seed records and is not a real event. first-hand-participant means the contributor was involved. public-reporting-reconstruction means rebuilt from published sources. contributor-composite means several real events merged to prevent identification.

title.description: Plain statement of what happened. No company, product, or person names.

date.description: When the incident occurred. A single partial date, or an object with start and end for incidents that ran over a period.

start.description: First date the failure was active.

sector.description: Sector of the organization that deployed the agent. Use a coarse sector, never a sub-niche that identifies the organization.

agent_type.description: The job the agent was doing when it failed, not the model or framework behind it.

autonomy_level.description: How much authority the agent had in the failing workflow. recommend-only: a person did every action. act-with-approval: the agent acted after a person approved each action. act-with-review: the agent acted and a person reviewed afterward. act-autonomously: the agent acted with no routine human review.

failure_types.description: One to three tags from taxonomy.md. Must include primary_failure_type.

primary_failure_type.description: The tag whose missing control, if present and working, would have prevented the harm. Use the tie-break rule in taxonomy.md. Must also appear in failure_types.

narrative.description: Anonymized account of what happened, 150 to 300 words (checked by scripts/validate.py). Sequence of events, no blame, no names, no identifying system details.

severity.description: low: contained internally, little cost. moderate: noticeable cost or customer effect, recovered within days. high: material financial, regulatory, or customer harm. critical: safety harm, large regulatory consequence, or loss that threatens the business unit.

description.description: What the impact was, using ranges or aggregate numbers rather than exact figures.

root_cause.description: The condition that made the failure possible. State the system or process cause, not a model quality complaint and not a person.

control_category.description: Family the missing control belongs to.

missing_control.description: The specific control that did not exist or did not operate, phrased as a control someone could implement.

description.description: Why the control was absent: not designed, designed but not built, built but bypassed, or built but not owned.

method.description: How the failure was first noticed.

time_to_detect.description: Elapsed time from first harmful action to detection.

lessons_learned.description: Two to five lessons, each a concrete change an organization could make.
